per year.150 Th e most common causes of SBS are malignancy, 
damage from radiation therapy (radiation enteritis), Crohn’s
disease with resulting multiple resections, vascular accident,
trauma, or volvulus.142, 151
Etiology Surgical resections of the small intestine and colon 
due to disease and trauma can result in extensive loss of surface 
area of the small intestine and colon. Without normal anatomy 
and physiology, malabsorption of nutrients, ﬂ uids, and electro-
lytes will result (see Tables 15.19 and 15.20).
